newsitem.title: USA: Dow index punches through 7,300 level for first time.
newsitem.headline: Dow index punches through 7,300 level for first time.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average punched through the 7,300-point level for the first time Tuesday, propelled by a big gain in International Business Machines Corp.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 21.43 points at 7,314.18 after closing Monday at a record high of 7,292.75.
But in the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on active volume of 284 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index slipped 0.62 of a point 1,343.57.
The modest gains of the blue-chip Dow index contrasted with Monday's 123-point jump, which capped a rise of more than 200 points in the past three sessions.
"Obviously, this momentum is not going to keep going the way it's been going, so there's going to be a lot of give and take," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage.
IBM, fresh off the victory of its Deep Blue supercomputer over world chess champion Garry Kasparov, was trading above its all-time high of 175-7/8.
IBM rose 2-5/8 to 176-1/8, getting a boost from a Goldman Sachs analyst who added the stock to the firm's recommended list.
One technology trader said that if IBM closes either at or above its historic highs, it could fuel even more momentum.
Wall Street cleared the first of three major economic data hurdles unscathed Tuesday when a report on retail sales for April came in generally as expected.
Retail sales fell 0.3 percent and 0.1 percent excluding autos. But the market-friendly data caused little immediate reaction in either the stock or bond markets.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury was off 2/32, leaving its yield steady at 6.89 percent.
"Bonds are probably more concerned with the statistics that are coming up ahead," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
On Wednesday, the government will issue its Producer Price Index report for April and the next day, the Consumer Price Index.
The wholesale and retail inflation data will be the last major economic information the markets will have before the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting next Tuesday.
General Motors Corp. was off 1-3/8 to 56-7/8. PaineWebber downgraded the stock and Goldman Sachs removed it from its 'Private Client Focus Portfolio,' replacing it with IBM.

Procter & Gamble Co. signed a deal to pay Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc. $135 million over five years as part of a venture to develop and sell pharmaceutical products. Regeneron shot up 3-7/8 to 11-3/4, while Procter & Gamble slipped 7/8 to 132-7/8.
